summary: The Playwright tests compile and use APIs correctly with awaited assertions, preserving test case IDs. However, selector quality is weak due to placeholder regex selectors ('category name'), generic selectors (h1), and assumptions without verification about the page content and product-category relationship. Assertions on page title and product relevance require stronger selectors or additional validation. There is no test data handling or reuse of selectors which impacts maintainability and reusability.

issues.description: The usage of /category name/i as a regex selector for role=link is a placeholder and weak. It may not uniquely identify the category link and could lead to flaky tests.
issues.recommendation: Replace with a specific and stable selector such as a data-test-id attribute or exact text matching the category name.

issues.description: Assertions rely on generic elements like 'h1' to verify category page display and page title containing 'Category Name' without verifying actual selected category or products belonging to the category.
issues.recommendation: Add assertions verifying the actual category name displayed on page and validate products belong to the clicked category, possibly via attributes or text content.

issues.description: Repeated navigation and locator logic is duplicated in each test, reducing maintainability and reusability.
issues.recommendation: Use test hooks or helper functions to navigate and get category links or product lists to improve code reuse and reduce duplication.

issues.description: No parameterization or external test data source is used; hardcoded assumptions are present.
issues.recommendation: Introduce external test data or test configuration for categories and expected results to make tests flexible and data-driven.

recommendations: Replace placeholder /category name/i selector with a precise stable selector.
Strengthen assertions to verify selected category and that products belong to it.
Refactor repeated navigation and selection logic into reusable functions or test hooks.
Consider adding data-driven test patterns for categories and products.
